--- Page 4 ---
<meta>This page is the beginning of the "Foreword" (Qianyan) for the 1988 reprint of the Daoist Canon. It follows the colophon and provides a historical and academic overview of the collection's significance, its origins, and its value to scholars beyond just religious study.</meta>

# Foreword

The Ming Dynasty *Zhengtong* edition of the **Daoist Canon** <note>original: "道藏" (Daozang). This refers to the massive 1445 collection compiled during the Zhengtong era.</note> contains 1,426 types of Daoist texts, totaling 5,305 volumes. These are organized into the "Three Grottoes," "Four Supplements," and "Twelve Categories." <note>These are the traditional hierarchical divisions used to classify the vast library of Daoist scripture.</note> The *Wanli* period **Supplement to the Daoist Canon** <note>The *Wanli Xu Daozang*, compiled in 1607.</note> added another 50 types of Daoist texts, totaling 180 volumes, which are no longer divided into categories. Together, the two parts of the *Daoist Canon* contain 1,476 types of Daoist texts across 5,485 volumes. This is the great collection of Daoist literature and a massive treasure house of our nation's traditional culture.

Daoism was formed during the reign of Emperor Shun of the Eastern Han Dynasty <note>approx. 125–144 CE</note> and is an indigenous religion of our country. Because it reveres Laozi (Li Er) as the founder of the religion and uses the *Classic of the Way and Virtue* (*Dao De Jing*) as its primary scripture, it is rooted in the Daoist philosophy of the Spring and Autumn period of the Eastern Zhou. Daoist philosophy also traces itself back to the Yellow Emperor <note>Huangdi, the legendary ancestor of Chinese civilization.</note>; by the Qin and Han periods, a **"Huang-Lao School"** <note>A school of thought combining the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi, focusing on governance and immortality.</note> had formed, which traced its theories and viewpoints back to the Yellow Emperor, the legendary representative of the beginnings of our national culture. In reality, the content of Daoism is diverse and eclectic. It merges ancient Chinese ideas of ghosts and spirits, shamanism, the arts of immortality, Lao-Zhuang Daoist philosophy, the "governance through non-action" (*wu-wei*) political thought of Huang-Lao, and the study of <term>chenwei: "apocryphal divinations," a system of mystical interpretations of the classics used for predicting the future or legitimizing rulers</term> that developed from the Yin-Yang and Five Elements theories of the pre-Qin period. Furthermore, at the time of its formation, it was integrated with contemporary peasant uprisings, and thus absorbed certain social ideals and political demands of the peasant masses, such as the idea of "Great Peace for Ten Thousand Years" (*wannian taiping*). Due to the inherent complexity of Daoism itself, the content of the *Daoist Canon* is extraordinarily diverse and vibrant.

The *Daoist Canon* includes many works on philosophy, military strategy, and medicine attributed to the Yellow Emperor; it includes the masterpieces and various commentaries of the Daoist masters; and it includes a vast amount of literature on Daoist doctrine, liturgical rites, talismans, biographies of immortals, and mountain gazetteers. Even **"Confucian books, medical books, works on Yin-Yang, divination, and the various schools of thought are all included within it."** <note>original: "儒书、医书、阴阳、卜筮、诸子百家皆与焉。" Quoted from the *Syllabus of the History of the Honored Scriptures of the Daoist Canon* from the Yuan Dynasty Zhiyuan period (1264–1294).</note> This unconventional inclusion of diverse books within the *Daoist Canon* was once criticized and ridiculed by both Confucian and Buddhist circles. The *General Catalog and Abstracts of the Siku Quanshu* <note>The "Complete Library of the Four Treasuries," a massive 18th-century imperial collection of Chinese literature.</note> attacked this heavily in its summary of the *Detailed Notes on the Table of Contents of the Daoist Canon*. However, many insightful scholars have always attached great importance to the various non-religious ancient books preserved in the *Daoist Canon*, using them as resources for collation, the recovery of lost ancient texts, and the study of ancient academic history. The famous Qing Dynasty scholar and founder of the Wu School of Han Learning, Hui Dong (1697–1758), once told the famous historian Qian Daxin (1728–1804): **"The Daoist Canon contains many ancient versions of Confucian books."** Qian noted these words and, in his later years, borrowed and read the Chaotian Palace edition of the *Daoist Canon* in Nanjing, and later the Xuanmiao Temple edition in Suzhou, discovering...

<summary>This page provides an introduction to the history and composition of the Daoist Canon, highlighting its status as a massive cultural repository that includes not only religious texts but also ancient works on medicine, philosophy, and military strategy.</summary>
<keywords>Daoist Canon, Daozang, Zhengtong era, Wanli era, Three Grottoes and Four Supplements, Huang-Lao School, Siku Quanshu, Hui Dong, Qian Daxin, textual criticism</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Daoist Canon's historical value for textual criticism and scholarship. # THE DAOIST CANON

...[he] discovered an important work on the geography of the Northwest and Central Asia, the **Travels of the Master of Eternal Spring to the West** <note>original: "長春真人西遊記" (Changchun zhenren xiyou ji). This text documents the journey of the Daoist master Qiu Chuji to meet Genghis Khan.</note> (found under the "Qun" category label). Bi Yuan (1730–1797), while collating the *Mozi* <note>A foundational text of Mohist philosophy from the 5th century BCE.</note> in the 48th year of the Qianlong reign (1783), used the version from the *Daoist Canon* for comparison. He noticed blank spaces in the text where characters were omitted to observe naming taboos from the Song Dynasty; from this, he knew the version in the *Canon* was derived from a Song-era edition. The following year (1784), while Zhuang Kuiji was collating the *Huainanzi*, he felt that the commentaries by Gao You had been heavily edited or deleted by later generations. He sought advice from the scholar Qian Dian (1744–1806), who told him: **"The version in the Daoist Canon is also not the complete original, but compared to the common editions circulating today, it contains fifty to sixty percent more material."** Consequently, Zhuang Kuiji went to the Nanshan Scripture Recitation Platform to study the *Daoist Canon*. During the Jiaqing reign (1796–1820), Sun Xingyan (1753–1818) printed the *Pingjinguan Collection*, in which he included several ancient lost books recovered from the *Daoist Canon*, such as the *Yellow Emperor’s Dragon-Head Classic*, the *Yellow Emperor’s Golden Casket and Jade Balance Classic*, the *Yellow Emperor’s Classic of the Mysterious Lady Bestowing Knowledge to Three Sons*, and the *Expanded Classic of the Yellow Emperor’s Conduct*. Yan Kejun (1762–1843), when compiling his massive anthology *Complete Library of Prose from High Antiquity, the Three Dynasties, Qin, Han, Three Kingdoms, and Six Kingdoms*, also made extensive use of the *Daoist Canon* to collect and collate lost fragments and surviving writings.

In modern times, several scholars have been very attentive to utilizing the *Daoist Canon* in their academic research. For instance, in the second year of the Xuantong reign (1910), Liu Shipei (1884–1919) studied the *Daoist Canon* at the White Cloud Temple in Beijing and wrote *Notes on Reading the Daoist Canon*. In the 20th year of the Republic (1931), Gu Jiegang (1893–1980) and Qu Jigao both studied the *Daoist Canon* at the Taiqing Palace on Mount Lao in Qingdao; Qu subsequently authored the book *A Brief Study of the Daoist Canon*. In the 31st year of the Republic (1942), Chen Guofu studied the *Daoist Canon* at the Peking University Humanities Research Institute in Longquan Town, Kunming. After many years of deep immersion, he conducted extensive scientific research on the formation and sects of Daoism, liturgical rituals, <term>waidan: "external alchemy," the practice of compounding elixirs using minerals and heat</term>, and <term>neidan: "internal alchemy," meditative practices involving breath and energy within the body</term>. This resulted in his work *Research on the Origins of the Daoist Canon*. All of this demonstrates that the *Daoist Canon* is not merely a collection of scriptures to be held and recited by "Yellow Caps" <note>a colloquial term for Daoist priests</note> or followed by practitioners.

Following the rise of Daoism, alchemists tracked the paths of the earlier <term>fangshi: "recipe masters" or practitioners of occult and technical arts</term> in search of immortality, smelting "elixirs of long life" and developing the **"Art of the Golden Elixir."** While their goal was spiritual, these actions unintentionally constituted a form of chemical experimentation. Throughout ancient Chinese and world history, they persisted in a movement of testing the chemical decomposition and synthesis of matter, leading to significant inventions. For example, black gunpowder—one of the four great inventions of ancient China—was, in terms of its origin, the byproduct of a failed alchemical experiment. When alchemists heated niter, charcoal, sulfur, and arsenic together, the result was an explosion that destroyed the furnace and killed the practitioners. To serve as a warning, Daoists recorded this formula in a technical manual within the *Daoist Canon* titled the *Essential Summary of the Mysterious Way of the True Origin*. In doing so, they unexpectedly preserved precious historical data for the history of chemistry and invention. Within the "Class of Diverse Arts" in the "Grotto of Spirit" <note>Dongshen, one of the three main divisions of the Canon</note> section of the *Daoist Canon*, many works describing various chemical experiments are indeed preserved. Examples include the *Thirty-Six Aqueous Methods*, a work on experiments involving various solutions soluble in water, and the *Record of Suspension and Solution*, which documents experiments in equilibrium and reduction.

<summary>This page highlights how the Daoist Canon served as a vital resource for Qing and modern scholars to recover lost ancient texts and documents the Canon's unintended role in the birth of chemistry and the invention of gunpowder.</summary>
<keywords>textual criticism, Bi Yuan, Sun Xingyan, Chen Guofu, external alchemy (waidan), internal alchemy (neidan), gunpowder, history of science, Thirty-Six Aqueous Methods</keywords>

# PREFACE

However, all of these traditions appeared in the form of the **"Art of the Golden Elixir,"** specifically **"external alchemy."** <term>waidan: "external alchemy," the practice of compounding elixirs using minerals and heat</term> The **"Art of the Golden Elixir"** also includes the methods of **"internal alchemy,"** <term>neidan: "internal alchemy," meditative practices involving breath and energy within the body</term> which uses the human body as the furnace to refine energy and cultivate truth: **"Refining essence to transform it into energy (qi), refining energy to transform it into spirit, refining spirit to return to the void, and becoming an immortal or a realized being."** <note>original: "煉精化氣，煉氣化神，煉神還虛，成仙成真." This summarizes the four stages of internal alchemical transformation.</note> Within the *Daoist Canon*, works such as the *Secret Formulas for Ascending to Perfection*, the *Record of Cultivating Nature and Extending Life*, and the *Classic of Breath by Master Taiwu of Mount Song* are all essential texts in this field. The cultivation of truth through **"internal alchemy"** is, in reality, a practice of physiological hygiene and physical exercise; it can be viewed as the creation of biological-chemical experiments within the physiology of the body.

The compilation of Daoist books began during the Eastern Jin Dynasty (317–420). Ge Hong (283–363), in the "Chapter on Glimpsing the Distant" within the *Inner Chapters of the Master Who Embraces Simplicity*, recorded the titles of Daoist books totaling 670 volumes, plus over 500 volumes of talismans and registers; the two categories together totaled 1,200 volumes. During the Liu Song period of the Southern Dynasties (420–479), the Daoist priest Lu Xiujing (406–477) searched for and collected texts even more extensively. He summarized them into the "Three Caverns" <note>The Three Caverns (Sandong) is the primary tripartite division of the Daoist Canon: the Grotto of Perfection, the Grotto of Mystery, and the Grotto of Spirit.</note> and, in the 7th year of the Taishi reign of Emperor Ming of Song (471), he presented the *Catalog of the Scriptural Books of the Three Caverns* to the throne by imperial decree.

The official organization of Daoist books into a "Canon" (Zang) began with Emperor Xuanzong (Li Longji) of the Tang Dynasty. During the Kaiyuan reign (713–741), he issued an imperial decree sending envoys to search for and collect Daoist scriptures. He personally inspected them and arranged the books into a "Canon" titled the *Three Caverns Net of Pearls*, totaling 3,744 volumes. In the 7th year of the Tianbao reign (748), he ordered copies to be made for wide distribution, naming it the *Kaiyuan Daoist Canon*. From this point on, Daoism and Buddhism each had their own "Canons" of scripture.

After the founding of the Zhao Song Dynasty (960–1279), the rulers also revered Daoism and made great efforts to collect Daoist books and compile a "Daoist Canon." In the early years of the Dazhong Xiangfu reign (1008–1016) of Emperor Zhenzong (Zhao Heng), an imperial decree was issued for Daoist priests to revise and check the texts. The Chancellor Wang Qinruo was appointed to oversee the project, which resulted in 4,359 volumes. He compiled a table of contents and presented it to the throne, where it was granted the name *Comprehensive Record of Treasured Writings*. Because there were many discrepancies within it, Wang Qinruo recommended Zhang Junfang to further edit and revise the collection. This resulted in a total of 4,565 volumes. The box labels were organized according to the *Thousand Character Classic* <note>A classic Chinese poem used as a primer for teaching characters; its unique sequence of characters was commonly used for filing and indexing.</note>, starting with the character "Heaven" (*tian*) and ending with the character "Palace" (*gong*), totaling 466 boxes. It was titled the *Grand Song Treasure Canon of the Celestial Palace*. By the 3rd year of the Tianxi reign of Emperor Zhenzong (1019), seven copies had been transcribed.

During the Chongning reign (1102–1106) of Emperor Huizong (Zhao Ji) of the Song Dynasty, another imperial decree was issued to search the empire for lost Daoist writings and order Daoist priests to edit them. During the Zhenghe reign (1111–1118), the Canon was carved onto printing blocks, totaling 540 boxes and 5,481 volumes, named the *Zhenghe Eternal Life Daoist Canon*. This was the beginning of the use of woodblock printing for the entire Daoist Canon. No printed copies of the *Zhenghe Daoist Canon* survive today.

In the 1st year of the Mingchang reign (1190) of Emperor Zhangzong (Wanyan Jing) of the Jin Dynasty <note>The Jin or "Jurchen" Dynasty, which ruled northern China while the Song ruled the south.</note>, an imperial decree was issued to carve and print a "Daoist Canon." It was completed two years later, totaling 6,455 volumes, and was called the *Great Jin Treasure Canon of the Mysterious Capital*. The printing blocks were stored at the Tianchang Temple in Beijing. In the 2nd year of the Taihe reign (1202), a fire broke out at the Tianchang Temple, and the printing blocks were destroyed. No printed copies of the Jin Canon survive today.

<summary>This page explains the shift from external chemical alchemy to internal physiological cultivation (neidan) and provides a chronological history of the Daoist Canon's compilation and printing from the 4th century through the 13th century.</summary>
<keywords>internal alchemy (neidan), Ge Hong, Lu Xiujing, Emperor Xuanzong, Three Caverns, Kaiyuan Daoist Canon, woodblock printing, Zhenghe Eternal Life Daoist Canon, Jin Dynasty</keywords>

# THE DAOIST CANON

At the beginning of the Mongol rise, the Great Progenitor Borjigin Temüjin (Genghis Khan) revered Daoism. He summoned the Perfected Man of Eternal Spring, Qiu Chuji (1148–1227), to the Snowy Mountains and honored him as an immortal. The Daoist priest Song Defang received imperial orders to search for and carve woodblocks for Daoist scriptures. By the third year of the regency of Empress Töregene (1244), the entire Canon was completed, totaling more than 7,800 volumes. The printing blocks were stored at the Temple of the Mysterious Capital in Yongle Town, Pingyang Prefecture (modern-day Shanxi Province, 60 kilometers southeast of Yongji County); this collection is also known as the **"Treasure Canon of the Mysterious Capital."**

After the founding of the Yuan Dynasty, Emperor Shizu (Kublai Khan) revered and trusted the leader of Lamaism, Phags-pa. During a debate between Buddhists and Daoists in the 17th year of the Zhiyuan reign (1280), the Daoists were defeated. Consequently, the Emperor ordered the burning of the printing blocks of the *Daoist Canon*. All Daoist books and scriptures, with the exception of the *Classic of the Way and Virtue* (Dao De Jing), suffered a terrible fate. Following the total destruction of the Yuan *Daoist Canon*, the only surviving printed editions were two works: the *Seven Slips from a Cloudy Shelf* <note>original: "雲笈七籤" (Yunji Qiqian). This is a famous anthology often called the "Mini-Daoist Canon" because it preserved essential texts.</note> and the *Scripture of the Wind and Dew of Great Purity*. Both are currently held in the Beijing Library. The *Seven Slips from a Cloudy Shelf* corresponds to the sections marked from "Study" (*xue*) to "Pear" (*tang*) in the later *Zhengtong Canon*, and several individual printed editions also exist. The *Scripture of the Wind and Dew of Great Purity*, in one volume, is attributed to the Perfected Man of No-Abiding; it is a truly unique Daoist scripture. This scripture is listed in the *Catalog of Missing Scriptures from the Daoist Canon*, proving that it was recorded as a missing work by comparing it with the "Mongol Canon" catalog when the *Zhengtong Canon* blocks were being carved.

No complete sets of the Song, Jin, or Mongol editions of the *Daoist Canon* have survived. The Qing Dynasty never carved a complete Canon. Therefore, the *Daoist Canon* and the *Supplement to the Daoist Canon* carved during the Zhengtong and Wanli reigns of the Ming Dynasty are the only complete versions of the *Daoist Canon* extant today.

At the beginning of the reign of Emperor Chengzu (Zhu Di) of the Ming Dynasty, he issued an imperial decree to the 43rd <term>Tianshi: "Celestial Master," the hereditary leader of the Zhengyi branch of Daoism</term>, Zhang Yuchu, to compile and edit the *Daoist Canon*. In the 8th year of the Yongle reign (1410), Zhang Yuchu passed away, and a decree was issued for the 44th Celestial Master, Zhang Yuqing, to continue the work. It was not until the 9th year of the Zhengtong reign of Emperor Yingzong (1444) that the woodblocks began to be carved. The project was completed in the 10th year of the Zhengtong reign (1445), and it was named the **"Zhengtong Daoist Canon."** The entire Canon consists of 5,305 volumes. It used the *Thousand Character Classic* <note>As noted previously, this primer's character sequence was used as a filing system.</note> for its box labels, starting with the character "Heaven" (*tian*) and ending with the character "Hero" (*ying*), totaling 480 boxes. Each box contains several volumes, and each volume is one physical book.

In the 35th year of the Wanli reign (1607) of the Ming Dynasty, the 50th Celestial Master, Zhang Guoxiang, received orders from Emperor Shenzong (Zhu Yijun) to proofread and carve the **"Supplement to the Daoist Canon."** This was intended to add Daoist books that were missing from the *Zhengtong Daoist Canon*, as well as Daoist works written after the Zhengtong era. It consists of 180 volumes and also follows the sequence of the *Thousand Character Classic*. It follows the *Zhengtong Daoist Canon*, starting from the character "Stop" (*du*) and ending with the character "Tassel" (*ying*), totaling 32 boxes.

Once the printing of the Ming Canon was finished, copies were distributed to famous mountains and temples throughout the country. One copy survived at the White Cloud Temple in Beijing. During the Daoguang reign of the Qing Dynasty (1821–1850), it was discovered that parts were missing or damaged. Zheng Yongxiang raised funds to hand-copy the missing sections, and the work was completed in the 25th year of the Daoguang reign (1845). He wrote the *Record of the Restoration of the Daoist Canon at the White Cloud Temple* to commemorate the event.

<summary>This page details the destruction of earlier Daoist Canons under the Mongol-Yuan Dynasty and the subsequent compilation of the Zhengtong and Wanli editions during the Ming Dynasty, which remain the only complete versions of the Daoist scriptures surviving today.</summary>
<keywords>Genghis Khan, Qiu Chuji, Phags-pa, book burning, Zhengtong Daoist Canon, Supplement to the Daoist Canon, Zhang Yuchu, White Cloud Temple, Celestial Master</keywords>

<meta>This page follows the history of the Daoist Canon into the modern era, detailing the 20th-century efforts to print facsimiles of the Ming Dynasty editions, the recovery of missing sections, and the discovery of ancient Daoist manuscripts at Dunhuang and Mawangdui.</meta>

<page-num>5</page-num>
-># PREFACE<-

From 1923 to 1926, the Hanfenlou <note>The famous library of the Commercial Press in Shanghai.</note> in Shanghai borrowed the *Zhengtong* and *Wanli* editions of the **"Daoist Canon"** and its **"Supplement"** held at the White Cloud Temple in Beijing to create a photostatic facsimile. Each set consisted of 1,120 volumes. At that time, the Beijing White Cloud Temple copy already had some missing parts, totaling ninety-eight leaves <note>In traditional Chinese binding, a "leaf" is a single sheet of paper folded to make two pages.</note>, which had not been found or replaced. In 1957, the Chinese Daoist Association of Taiwan initiated a reprint based on the Hanfenlou facsimile, which was completed in 1977. This version consisted of sixty volumes per set, with one volume for the catalog. The missing leaves were still not replaced, though fifteen types of lost Daoist books from the Ming and Qing Dynasties were added as a supplement.

Currently, to meet the research needs of the academic and religious communities, the Cultural Relics Publishing House, the Shanghai Bookstore, and the Tianjin Ancient Books Publishing House have collaborated to publish a new facsimile based on the original Hanfenlou edition. The missing leaves from the original Beijing White Cloud Temple copy were identified using the detailed lists compiled by Mr. Qu Fengqi (1908–1987) during his lifetime. These gaps were filled using the old collection of the Shanghai White Cloud Temple, now held in the Shanghai Library, finally making the work complete. (In total, more than 1,700 lines were supplemented, seventeen instances of misordered pages were corrected, and over 500 damaged or missing characters were restored.) Additionally, the *Detailed Annotations of the Catalog of the Daoist Canon* in four volumes, written by Bai Yunji of the Ming Dynasty, has been appended. This was printed using the Qing Dynasty woodblock edition once owned by Miao Quansun and now held in the Shanghai Library. This version is superior to the version in the *Complete Library of the Four Treasuries* <note>The "Siku Quanshu," a massive 18th-century imperial encyclopedia. The version mentioned here was a separate reprint by Xu Shichang.</note> because the imperial version lacks three sections—"The Origins of the Daoist School," "Editorial Principles," and the "General Catalog of the Daoist Canon"—and its annotations also have omissions. There is another Qing woodblock edition with a layout similar to the Miao collection copy, but the author's name was forged as "Li Jie of Liaozuo" (this is the version used in the *Essentials of the Daoist Canon*); it should be noted that this is a pseudonym.

Aside from the *Zhengtong Daoist Canon* and the *Wanli Supplement*, many Daoist books were never included. These include:
(1) Daoist books written after the Wanli reign of the Ming. For example, the **"Collected Essentials of the Daoist Canon"** compiled and carved by Peng Dingqiu during the Kangxi reign of the Qing Dynasty includes 110 types of Daoist books in 288 volumes written by authors of the late Ming and early Qing.
(2) Ancient Daoist scriptures missed by the *Zhengtong* and *Wanli* collections, such as the previously mentioned *Scripture of the Wind and Dew of Great Purity*.
(3) The massive cache of manuscripts discovered in 1899 in the Library Cave (Cave 17) of the Mogao Caves at Mount Mingsha, Dunhuang. Among these are approximately 500 volumes of Daoist books. Stolen by British and French explorers and now held in the British Museum and the National Library of France, works such as the *Xiang’er Commentary on the Laozi Daodejing* and the *Scripture of Laozi Converting the Barbarians* are extremely important Daoist documents.
(4) In 1973, during the excavation of the No. 3 Western Han Tomb at Mawangdui, Changsha, a large number of silk manuscripts were recovered. These included major works of the <term>Huang-Lao: A school of thought named after the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi) and Laozi that was influential in the early Han Dynasty.</term> tradition that had been lost for ages, such as *The Standards of Law*, *The Ten Great Classics*, *Balance*, and *The Source of the Way*.
(5) *The Great Canon of the Yongle Era*, which survived the looting of the Old Summer Palace. Although only 3.48% of the original 22,877 volumes remain, it is still possible to extract from the surviving volumes texts that were in the Zhengtong... <note>Text ends mid-sentence.</note>

<header>The Daoist Canon</header>

# THE DAOIST CANON

...Daoist books missing from the collected **"Daoist Canon."** For example, Volume 911 of the *Great Canon* <note>Referring to the "Yongle Dadian," the massive 15th-century encyclopedia mentioned on the previous page.</note> preserves two works: the *Scripture of the Five Refinements for Delivering the Corpse through the Mystery of the Numinous Treasure* and the *Great Emperor’s Method for Governing Souls and Subduing Corpses*. Volume 1,310 preserves the *Numinous Treasure Scripture on the Ritual Protocols of Bells and Chimes* and the *Numinous Treasure Scripture on the Ritual Protocols of the Three Origins*. All of these works await future systematic collection and publication.

->Hu Daojing, June 1987<-

It focuses on the "Registers" (Lu) of the Orthodox Unity (Zhengyi) tradition—which are essentially spiritual certificates of rank and protection—and the "Pure Rules" (Qinggui) and "Recorded Sayings" (Yulu) of the Quanzhen (Complete Perfection) school. This transition marks the move from theory and science into the lived institutional and liturgical practice of the Ming-era Daoist community.</meta>

# Wondrous Scripture of the Upper Chapters on Limitless Salvation of the Numinous Treasure, Volume 1
<note>The **Numinous Treasure** (Lingbao) is one of the primary schools of Daoism, focusing heavily on ritual and the universal salvation of all beings.</note>

<page-num>1 — 1</page-num>

->**Wondrous Scripture of the Upper Chapters on Limitless Salvation of the Numinous Treasure, Volume 1**<-

<meta>Woodblock print featuring fine-line illustrations and standard script text. Inscription dated to the 10th year of the Zhengtong era (1445) of the Ming Dynasty.</meta>

[A large woodcut illustration divided into two main panels. The upper panel depicts a celestial assembly with two central deities seated on elaborate thrones, surrounded by a multitude of smaller figures—deities, immortals, and attendants—amidst swirling clouds and divine light. The lower panel shows a central deity seated on a lion throne within a circular halo, also surrounded by a celestial host. To the left of this lower panel is an ornamental border containing an inscription.]

<insert>
Heaven and Earth are fixed in their positions; Yin and Yang are harmonized. The calendar unfolds in its proper order; the sun and moon shine with clarity.
The imperial ancestors are blessed with celebration; the western fields are tilled in their season. The mountain peaks soar high; the rivers and seas run clear and still.
The sagely transformation reaches everywhere; even the fish and turtles find their place. Families are harmonious and households are at peace; clothing and food are abundant.
Ritual and deference lead the way to benevolence; the spread of transformation is refined and bright. Customs are honest and kind; punishments and fines are no longer raised.
The imperial road is level and straight; the four barbarian tribes submit as guests. Neighboring countries are peaceful and secure; the ancestral shrines are held in high honor.
Ten thousand paths arrive at celebration; may the Emperor rule forever for ten thousand generations.
The tenth day of the tenth month of the tenth year of the Zhengtong era <note>Corresponding to November 9, 1445 CE.</note>.

# Wondrous Scripture of the Upper Chapters on Limitless Salvation of the Numinous Treasure, Volume 1
### Heaven One

The Dao says: Formerly, in the Heaven of Primordial Azure, within the empty songs of the Jade Void and the land of Great Fuli, the <term>Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning</term> <note>**Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning** (Yuanshi Tianzun) is the highest deity in the Lingbao tradition, representing the beginning of the universe.</note> received the Limitless Upper Chapters for the Salvation of Humanity. When the Celestial Worthy was about to speak this scripture, he circled ten times to summon the ten directions.

As he was about to take his seat, the Great Spirits of Heavenly Truth, the High Sovereigns of the Upper Saints, the Perfected Ones of Wondrous Conduct, and a countlessly large assembly came riding through the void. They arrived on flying clouds and cinnabar mists, in green carriages with jasper wheels. Feathered canopies cast shade over them, and flowing essences of jade-light in five colors glowed vibrantly, illuminating the great space of the void.

For seven days and seven nights, the sun, moon, and the rotating stars of the various heavens—the Jade Cross-bar and the Pearl Pivot—all stopped their rotations at once. The divine winds grew silent and still. The mountains and seas hid the clouds; the sky had no floating mists, and the four breaths were bright and clear. The entire land of the country, the mountains, rivers, forests, and trees, all became perfectly level, without any high or low places. Everything turned into green jade, with no variation in color.

The host of Perfected Ones stood in attendance around the throne. The Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning sat suspended in the empty void, atop a throne of five-colored lions.

When he spoke the scripture for the first time, the Great Saints of the various heavens all praised its goodness together. At that time, the deaf men and women of the country all had their ears opened.

When he spoke the scripture a second time, the blind were able to see clearly.

When he spoke the scripture a third time, the mute were able to speak.

When he spoke the scripture a fourth time, those with lameness or chronic disabilities were all able to stand and walk.

When he spoke the scripture a fifth time, those with long-standing or incurable diseases were instantly restored to health.

When he spoke the scripture a sixth time, white hair turned black again, and lost teeth regrew.

When he spoke the scripture a seventh time, the old became young again, and the young became strong.

When he spoke the scripture an eighth time, pregnant women and the gestating young of birds and beasts—whether already born or yet to be born—were all safely brought to completion.

When he spoke the scripture a ninth time, the treasuries of the earth opened up, revealing gold and jade.

When he spoke the scripture a tenth time, dry bones were brought back to life, rising up to become whole people again.

At that time, every man and woman in the country turned their hearts toward the teaching. All received protection and salvation, and all attained long life.

<summary>This page marks the beginning of the Scripture of Salvation, describing a cosmic event where the Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning reveals a text that cures all ailments and restores life to the dead. It is preceded by a Ming dynasty inscription praying for the longevity of the empire.</summary>

<keywords>Duren Jing, Lingbao, Yuanshi Tianzun, Zhengtong era, Daoist ritual, miracles, salvation, celestial assembly, Ming dynasty woodblock</keywords>

--- Page 45 ---
<meta>This page continues the narrative of the revelation of the Scripture of Salvation. Having described the healing miracles of the first ten recitations, it now details how the Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning summoned spirits from the ten directions and performed the miracle of the "Jewel Pearl," where the entire cosmic assembly was contained within a space no larger than a grain of millet.</meta>

<page-num>Heaven One — 3</page-num>
<header>The Daoist Canon</header>
<sig>1-11</sig>

The Dao says: At that time, the Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning spoke the scripture for the first time. From the Eastern Direction, a limitless and immeasurable multitude of Supreme Great Spirits of the highest rank arrived, floating through the void. When the ten recitations were complete, the Supreme Great Spirits of the Heavens from all ten directions arrived at once. The men and women of the entire country turned their hearts in devotion. Those who came were like fine rain or dense mist; the immeasurable multitude was so great that they crowded half the country, and the earth itself began to sink and tilt under their weight, impossible to prevent. 

Thereupon, the Primordial One suspended a **Jewel Pearl** <note>The **Jewel Pearl** (Baozhu) is a central symbol in Daoist mysticism, representing the "seed" of the universe—a microscopic point that contains the macroscopic totality of existence.</note>, as large as a grain of millet, in the center of the dark void, fifty feet above the ground. The people of the land looked up and saw them entering the mouth of the pearl in a bustling swarm. Once they had entered the mouth of the pearl, no one knew where they were. The people of the country then dispersed, and the earth returned to being level and upright, no longer narrow or sunken. Inside the Jewel Pearl, the Primordial One completed the recitation of the scripture. The Imperial Sovereigns of the various heavens then bestowed this teaching upon me. The entire land turned in devotion, and everyone practiced a heart of goodness. They did not kill or harm; they were not jealous or envious; they did not commit adultery or steal; they were not greedy or full of desire; they did not hate or act with malice. Their speech was without flowery deception, and their mouths uttered no evil sounds. They were united in compassion and love; even those of different lineages became as close as kin. The country was secure, and the people were prosperous, rejoicing in a reign of Great Peace. When the scripture first emerged as a teaching, the entire country followed the Dao. Those who possessed a determined heart and honored it with devotion all attained transcendence from the world.

# The Tenfold Merit of Scriptural Recitation for Establishing Virtue and Dispelling All Misfortune
### Universal Salvation Without End

The Way says: For those whose initial studies in the Way are shallow, or whose immortal rank is not yet fulfilled, they may face "extinction and deliverance" <note>A term for death, viewed as a transitional state in Daoist alchemy.</note>. When the body passes through the realm of Great Yin <note>The underworld or the grave.</note>, their fellow practitioners of the Way should offer incense and recite this scripture ten times on their behalf. This is done to deliver the "corpse-form." Following the proper law, the soul and spirit will proceed directly to the **Southern Palace** <note>The realm of ritual purification and rebirth.</note>. Based on the merit of their studies, the days will be counted until they attain rebirth. Turning through the cycles without being destroyed, they shall then attain the rank of Spirit Immortal.

The Way says: When the cycles of Heaven and Earth reach their end, one should also practice the fast, offer incense, and recite the scripture. When the constellations lose their degree or the sun and moon lose their light, one should also practice the fast, offer incense, and recite the scripture. When the four seasons lose their order or the Yin and Yang are not in harmony, one should also practice the fast, offer incense, and recite the scripture. If the ruler of the nation faces disaster or if military weapons rise in all directions, one should also practice the fast, offer incense, and recite the scripture. If plagues and poisons spread, and the common people suffer death and injury, one should also practice the fast, offer incense, and recite the scripture. When a teacher or a friend passes away, one should also practice the fast, offer incense, and recite the scripture. The merit of fasting and reciting the scripture is extremely heavy. Above, it dispels heavenly disasters and protects the Emperor; below, it wards off poisonous harms to save the masses. Both the living and the dead rely upon it; its blessings are difficult to surpass. Thus it is called the "Limitless Universal Salvation of Heavens and Humans."

The Way says: Whoever possesses this scripture and is able to perform this merit for the sake of Heaven, Earth, the Emperor, and the people—on days of disaster, if they set their heart to practice the fast, burn incense, and recite the scripture ten times, the various heavens will record their name, and ten thousand spirits will stand guard. They will be set apart as a Perfected One, surely becoming a minister of the Golden Court of the Saintly Sovereign. The various heavens record human merits and faults without the slightest error. Even the Demon Kings of the heavens will protect your body. Those who attain the Way are those who have understood these most high words.

The Great Spirit of the Eastern Sovereign <note>The spirit associated with the element of Wood and the direction of the East.</note> maintains the Wood-order, washing away and quieting the realms. The Great Spirit of the Southern Perfected One calms the extremes of fiery disasters. The Great Spirit of the White Emperor <note>Associated with the element of Metal and the West.</note> eliminates and transforms the weapons of war. The Great Spirit of the Primordial Crystal <note>Associated with the element of Water and the North.</note> merges the virtues of the mysterious gathering. The Great Spirit of the Central Sovereign generally governs the talismans and spirits.

The spirits of the Five Directions, Ten Realms, and Ten Thousand Ways hold the ritual bells and wield the battle-axes, standing in solemn guard by the millions. They drum the movement of the net of transformation, and their names command the spirits and the Perfected. Throughout the cycles of the aeons, they preserve and stabilize Heaven and Earth so they do not tilt. The Twenty-Eight Constellations <note>The traditional divisions of the Chinese sky.</note> resist the "four frosts" of chaos. The Middle Dipper <gloss>Nine</gloss> faces forward to stop disasters and open the way for life. The four seasons are arranged in order; cold and heat circulate, and Yin and Yang rotate.

Let no strange calamities interfere. When the great aeon reaches its term, they repel the crowds of disasters. The Master of the Five Rivers, the Great Spirit of Extended Cold, urges the inspection and recording of deeds, opening and clearing the paths of the water. The Talisman of the Primordial Beginning <note>Yuanshi: The supreme deity representing the origin of the universe.</note> proclaims: should any spirit dare to delay, they shall be sent to the high officials for execution, leaving no trace. The treacherous and evil lose their spirit; the roots of demonic vapors are destroyed. The world receives great blessings, and the Dao’s transformation becomes clear and pure.

The people carry the celebration of prosperity; benevolence and goodness flourish. All wonders are promoted together, ascending to the Upper Palace. In accordance with the cycles of time, they are presented to the High Void. The Great Brahma <term>Dafan: the primordial, creative sound or breath of the universe</term> of the Primordial Beginning extends the Three Breaths, dividing the two images <note>Yin and Yang.</note> and establishing the ten thousand heavens. Spirits are spread like a net, and the creation of life is nurtured. The Five Breaths circulate, and the Six Breaths take their turns in succession. Prosperity and decline follow one another.

When the cosmic breath is blocked, the great aeons become entangled. Life has its destined meetings with the disasters of Water, Fire, and Wind <note>The forces believed to destroy the world at the end of a cosmic cycle.</note>. The brilliance of the spirits is extinguished, and the three lights <note>Sun, Moon, and Stars.</note> hide their glow. Good and evil are indistinguishable, and misfortune and blame race together. Yet the Primordial Beginning settles the realms, and the merit of blessings arises naturally. The Great Seal-script of the Spirit Book, the Upper Chapter of the Precious Record, summons the great spirits of the ten directions.

The banners are raised and the charts are established, unceasing and eternal. The towering Qi of the Dao opens the path for wondrous use. The divine net of the cosmic warp and woof turns the Dharma-wheel of the aeons. The pivot of creation preserves the original purity. The spiritual wind fans the eight reaches into peace and harmony. The breath is infused with goodness and auspicious omens arrive. The celestial administration is proclaimed, passing through the High Perfected of the Qin. Within the "Perfected" is the Great Sovereign of Long Life, the Later Saint of the Divine Empyrean, and the Sovereign of Green Radiance.

The immortal officials of the Eastern Pole and the Western Terrace, on the left and right, hold the talismans and fix the registers to preserve the State of Mystery <term>Xiyi: a state of subtle, imperceptible existence</term>. The majestic and bright talisman-officers stop all errors. Above, they serve the Nine Heavens; below, they control the Three Disasters. Across the four dimensions and eight regions, all virtue returns. Evil and filth are washed away; demons and plagues are crushed. For millions of years, there is wealth, joy, and peace. No room is left for the wicked; supreme goodness is renewed daily. The loyal and the good assist in the transformation, matching the brilliance of the Dao. The Dao penetrates and extends through immeasurable aeons of salvation, removing disasters. The winds and fires do not stop, but the seas and the universe are tranquil and the heavens and earth are clear. The celebration of destiny reaches the deep ancestors; the coffins of the dead are washed clean, souls are released from their debts, and grievances are resolved. Pure transformation spreads, as all the heavens offer praise. The Great Saints of all the heavens are filled with joy. At the center is the "Song of the Empty Cavern," and the "Spirit Chapters of the Demon Kings," whose words participate in the High Truth.

### I. The Sound of Flying Through the Eternal Aeon in the Realm of Desire <term>Yujie: the lowest of the Three Realms, characterized by sensory attachment</term>

> Good fortune and celebration are just beginning.
> The way of evil is destroyed by me,
> And auspicious signs arrive.
> The Way of Heaven is clear and bright;
> The vapor of calamity is cut off.
> Benevolence and goodness return to the highest virtue,
> While the mountain of wickedness creates evil roots.
> Those with greedy love forget to guard the truth;
> Their path through the heavenly scriptures is erroneous <gloss>Heaven Four</gloss>.
> Do not let them become a flowery error;
> One must preserve Great Peace.
> Evil demons delight in cruelty and theft;
> They injure and exhaust the living souls.
> They disturb my realm of pure stillness,
> Indulging in poison and suffering.
> The High Sovereign, King of Pure Kings,
> Grants me the Chapter of the Numinous Treasure.
> It restrains and controls throughout long aeons;
> One always receives the peerless merit.
> Since the true wind is vast and wide,
> The prosperity of the world flourishes day by day.

### The True Talisman for Preserving the World of the Celestial Worthy of Great Peace and National Protection

<image-desc>A rectangular frame containing a complex Taoist talisman (Fu). It consists of three vertical columns of sigils, combining calligraphic swoops, abstract geometry, and pseudo-characters intended to represent celestial commands.</image-desc>

The three talismans mentioned above should be cast in gold or bronze and placed above the gates and corridors of the palace for great auspiciousness. Those who study the Dao should wear them to extend their years, reject disasters, and cross over difficulties. They may also be written with cinnabar on red paper according to the regulations.

---

Above these Three Realms, in the midst of the flying void, are the sounds of the "hidden names" of the True Demons. These sounds participate in the "Chapters of the Cavern." One who receives them will forever extend their fated cycle, and the Emperor’s throne will flourish. Reciting them one hundred times eliminates seasonal disasters. Reciting them one thousand times causes the Demon Kings to guard the saintly. Reciting them ten thousand times allows one to communicate with the immortals. For a hundred million generations, there shall be peace and prosperity, preserving and delivering through the transformations of the aeons. Even if ten thousand mountains were to collapse, upon hearing these spiritual sounds, the Demon Kings will respect the form. They command the Earth Spirits to stand guard, and the divine Perfected, officials, and citizens will be healthy and happy, escaping from disasters and hardships.

---

Great blessings and celebrations arrive; none fail to reach them. This is what is called infinite preservation and endless salvation. These are the secret writings of the upper heavens, revered by all the heavens together. To leak them or treat them with slow disrespect will lead to falling into hell, with misfortune reaching back to the ancestors.

The Dao says: These two chapters are both the secret, hidden sounds of the High Emperors of the various heavens and the Great Spiritual Demon Kings. They are all words of the Great Brahma <note>original: "Dafan"</note> that assist the fate of the aeons, guard the world, and send down auspiciousness. <gloss>Twenty-four</gloss> The beat is true and saves the spirit; it benefits the people and brings peace to the state. The words have no ornate rhythm and the melodies have no flowery embellishments, thus they are called "mysterious and profound," difficult to investigate in detail. They are the treasures of the upper heavens, kept secret in the Jade Offices and flowery halls of the Jade Purity within the Divine Empyrean. They are passed down once every sixty thousand aeons. If there is a "Perfected Person" <term>Zhiren: a high-ranking Daoist initiate</term> who offers inner treasures and whose heart follows the old rules and oaths to the Nine Heavens, then these may be transmitted to them.

The Dao says: The cycles of Heaven and Earth have periods of blockage and endings; the Sun, Moon, and Five Planets have periods of waning and waxing. The number of the aeons and the cycles of the world have periods of contraction and extension. Even the Highest Sage and Divine Beings have periods of rest and failure; even the followers of later studies have periods of sickness and injury. Whenever these disasters occur, those of the same breath should all unify their hearts, perform the fasts, offer incense at the six appointed times, and turn the scripture ten times. Merit and virtue will descend immediately, eliminating all inauspiciousness. The text of the "Infinite" universally saves without end.

The Dao says: If those of later studies have shallow Dao, or their immortal rank is not yet filled, and their cycle responds to "extinction and delivery" <note>Death.</note> as the body’s aeon reaches its end: when the time comes to pass through the Great Yin <note>The underworld or the state of being deceased.</note>, fellow "Perfected" should offer incense for them and recite the scripture ten times to deliver the corpse-form. Just as in the "Method of the Five Refinings of the Living Corpse," the soul and spirit will go directly to the Southern Palace <note>The celestial realm of rebirth and transformation.</note>. Their name will be recorded by the Mysterious Elder of the Celestial Mechanism. Based on the merit of their studies, the days will be calculated and they shall obtain rebirth in the turning wheel without confusion, immediately obtaining the status of a Divine Immortal.

The Dao says: When the cycles of Heaven and Earth reach their end, one should perform the fasts, offer incense, and recite the scripture. When the stars are in disorder and the sun and moon lose their light, one should perform the fasts, offer incense, and recite the scripture. When the four seasons lose their measure and Yin and Yang are not in harmony, one should perform the fasts, offer incense, and recite the scripture. When the great and small aeons end, the five cycles change, and the generations continue, one should perform the fasts, offer incense, and recite the scripture. When plagues and poisons spread, and millions of people are killed or injured, one should perform the fasts, offer incense, and recite the scripture. When the harvests do not ripen, one should perform the fasts, offer incense, and recite the scripture. The merit of fasting and reciting the scripture <gloss>Thirteen</gloss> is extremely heavy. Above, it eliminates celestial disasters and preserves the sovereign; below, it repels poisonous harms to deliver the millions of citizens. The living and the dead receive and rely on its blessings, which are difficult to surpass. Thus it is called "Infinitely and Universally Saving Celestials and Humans."

The Dao says: Whenever this scripture exists, it can perform this merit for Heaven, Earth, the Sovereign, and the people. On days of disaster, if one makes the resolution to perform the fast, burn incense, and recite the scripture ten times, all the heavens will record the name, and ten thousand spirits will stand guard. This distinguishes the "Perfected Person" who is destined to become a minister of the Golden Gate and a Sage Lord. The various heavens record human merit and error to the smallest fraction without mistake. The Demon Kings of the heavens also protect and recommend your person. One who obtains the Dao shall clearly understand these ultimate words.

### The Eight Heavens of the North
The net of light shakes the vastness; Knotted foam sinks into the sea; Sleeves of the mound simulate the net.

The Dao says: These "Hidden Sounds of the Great Brahma" <note>original: "Dafan Yinyu"</note> and "Infinite Tones" within the various heavens were originally written in characters ten feet wide. The True Imperial Man of the Heavens carved these texts onto tablets of crimson jade to serve as the "Correct Sounds." They are distributed across the terraces, watchtowers, and the chambers of the Palace of Great Tenuity and Purple Tenuity. They serve to control the large and small aeon-cycles, the counts of the world, and the cycles of water and fire. If there is one who knows these sounds and is able to fast and recite them, the various heavens will send "Sky-Flying Spirit Kings" down to observe their person and record their diligent merit. This is reported upward to the various heavens and the ten thousand spirits. The Earth Deities will pay homage at their gate. Through great merit, the True Kings will recommend them for promotion to the upper immortals. Once their Dao is complete, they may travel through the Three Realms and enter the Golden Gate. These sounds are such that there is nothing they cannot repel, nothing they cannot drive away, nothing they cannot deliver, and nothing they cannot complete. They are the natural sounds of the Celestial Truth. Thus, reciting them causes the "Sky-Flying" spirits to descend and observe; the High Emperor chants from afar, and the ten thousand spirits pay homage. The Three Realms attend the carriage. In the autumn of the masses, with the spirit focused on the East, the "Essence" naturally vanishes. The tinkling of jade resounds; the ten directions are solemn and clear. The rivers and seas are silent, and the mountain peaks swallow the mist. The ten thousand numina are subdued, and the various immortals are summoned. The heavens have no foul vapors, the earth has no dust. Dark wisdom pierces the clarity; great abundance in the mysterious of the mysteries.

# The Numinous Treasure Sublime Scripture of Infinite Salvation, Volume 5

## Chapter on Eliminating and Averting Disasters for National Sovereigns, Marquises, and the World's Lands
<gloss>Heaven Five</gloss>

The Dao says: Formerly, in the Heaven of Stillness and Remoteness, within the Great True Land of Joy of the Jade Scenery, I received the "Infinite Supreme Chapter of the Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning for Eliminating and Averting Disasters for National Sovereigns, Marquises, and the World's Lands." When the Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning was about to speak this scripture, it was circulated ten times to summon the ten directions. He first took his seat among the Great Divine Spirits of the Celestial Truth, the High Sages and Exalted Ones, the Shining Treasure Perfected Persons, the Immortal Kings of the various heavens, the Dukes and Marquises of the Taiji, the Immortal Elders of the Left and Right, the Ministers, and the Divine Officials—an innumerable multitude. They arrived riding through the air on jeweled silken ropes and celestial horses, in cloud-chariots of flowing essence, with radiant splendor and flowery shoes. They shone like floating gold, shaking the fruit-laden branches as their wheels turned. Five-colored clouds reflected upon each other, and the attending stars were spread like a net. The Nine Numinous Spirits opened auspiciousness, and the Eight Voids were pierced by the light. For seven days and seven nights, the immortals and perfected of the various heavens and the Three Realms were simultaneously delivered into joy. The multitude of perfected harmonized their virtue; humans and devas were healthy and peaceful. The poison of disasters was extinguished and transformed into the joy of Great Peace <term>Taiping: the ideal state of cosmic and social harmony</term>. The lands, mountains, rivers, forests, and trees of the various heavens became level and equal, with no more high or low. The earth all became yellow jade, without any different colors. The various perfected sat in attendance as the Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning sat in the mysterious void, floating upon the nine-light jeweled algae and the Great Harmony Jade Dragon.

When the scripture was recited once, the Great Sages of the various heavens simultaneously praised its goodness. At that time, throughout the lands of the universal heavens, the wind and transformation were peaceful and clear. 

When the scripture was recited twice, strange and monstrous portents were no longer born. 

When the scripture was recited three times, the seasons and order reached harmony and peace. 

When the scripture was recited four times, the stars and constellations followed their proper orbits, and the sun and moon shone constantly. 

When the scripture was recited five times, the five grains reached maturity, and the vegetation was lush without any violent blight. 

When the scripture was recited six times, the people preserved the truth and abandoned falsehood, and their hearts were free from desiring thoughts. 

When the scripture was recited seven times, the people's virtue returned to benevolence, and they enjoyed wealth, longevity, and health. 

When the scripture was recited eight times, the Correct Dao flourished everywhere, and all living beings returned to their true nature.

# The Numinous Treasure Sublime Scripture of Infinite Salvation, Volume 5

### [Top Register]

When the scripture is recited nine times, national sovereigns and imperial lords will have their longevity increased by ten thousand years. When the scripture is recited ten times, the heavens and humanity celebrate together, and the blessings of the throne are infinite. At that time, every man and woman in the nation will devote their hearts, gratefully receiving protection and deliverance, and all shall attain long life.

The Dao says: At that time, the Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning recited the scripture once. From the Eastern Boundless region, a countless multitude of Great Sages and High Deities of Disaster Elimination arrived, floating through the air. 

When the scripture was recited twice, from the Southern Boundless region, a countless multitude of Great Sages and High Deities of Warding Calamity arrived, floating through the air. 

When the scripture was recited three times, from the Western Boundless region, a countless multitude of Great Sages and High Deities of Scattering Misfortune arrived, floating through the air. 

When the scripture was recited four times, from the Northern Boundless region, a countless multitude of Great Sages and High Deities of Removing Evil arrived, floating through the air. 

When the scripture was recited five times, from the Northeastern Boundless region, a countless multitude of Great Sages and High Deities of Destroying the Hideous <note>original: "Miezhou," referring to monstrous or unsightly demonic influences</note> arrived, floating through the air. 

When the scripture was recited six times, from the Southeastern Boundless region, a countless multitude of Great Sages and High Deities of Decapitating Evil arrived, floating through the air. 

When the scripture was recited seven times, from the Southwestern Boundless region, a countless multitude of Great Sages and High Deities of Cleansing Filth arrived, floating through the air. 

When the scripture was recited eight times, from the Northwestern Boundless region, a countless multitude of Great Sages and High Deities of Thwarting Heresy arrived, floating through the air. 

When the scripture was recited nine times, from the Boundless region Above, a countless multitude of Great Sages and High Deities of Exterminating Pestilence arrived, floating through the air.
<gloss>Heaven Five: One</gloss>

When the scripture was recited ten times, from the Boundless region Below, the Great Sages and High Deities of Subduing Demons arrived with a countless multitude, floating through the air. 

When the ten recitations were completed, the most true High Deities of the ten boundless directions who eliminate and ward off all calamities and omens in the world arrived simultaneously. The lords, ministers, and the millions of people of the various celestial kingdoms turned their hearts in devotion, arriving like rushing clouds and gathering mists. This countless multitude traveled through the land until it was level; where the earth had been sunken or broken, it was restored, and nothing could obstruct them.

### [Middle Register]

Then, the Primordial Beginning transformed into a single Divine Pearl <note>This represents the "Millet Seed," a Taoist symbol for the microscopic point from which the entire universe originates</note>, as large as a grain of millet. Its condensed radiance was brilliant and shimmering, rising and falling, hovering in the Great Void. The Primordial Beginning drew it in, and its flowery rays reached everywhere. 

All the Celestial Truths, Great Deities, Upper Sages, Exalted Ones, Radiant Treasure Perfected Persons, and the countless multitudes of High Deities of the ten boundless directions who ward off the world's calamities—along with the lords, ministers, and millions of people of the various celestial kingdoms—all entered into the Divine Pearl. 

The deas and humans looked up and saw only the kingdoms of the various heavens, the lords, ministers, and people, and the deities who ward off the world's calamities. They saw them moving in vast numbers within the flowery radiance. Once they had entered the radiance, no one knew where they were. The people of the nations were dispersed into the void, and the earth returned to being level and upright, no longer tilted or sunken. 

The Primordial Beginning then spoke the scripture from within the Divine Pearl. When it was finished, the Perfected Essence was established and delivered, and it was bestowed upon me. At that time, the joy and celebration were beyond words. The ritual matters were briefly completed, and the various heavens returned to their positions. In an instant, it was silent, with no lingering sound. 

At that time, the devas and humans who encountered this scriptural law all attained salvation. They completed their natural lifespans without any injury or harm. The world was at peace, and everything flourished. There was no disturbance or competition, no sickness or injury, no punishment or killing, no intrusion or theft. None were untimely lost or held in low estate. High and low shared a single virtue, preserving Great Harmony. They were unified in compassionate love; even those of different lineages became like kin <note>original: "yigu chengqin," literally "different bones become relatives"</note>. The country was secure, the people prosperous, and all rejoiced in Great Peace <term>Taiping: a state of perfect cosmic and social equilibrium</term>. As the scripture first emerged to teach, the ten thousand nations followed the Dao. Those who possessed a sincere heart to honor and worship it all attained deliverance from the world.
<gloss>Heaven Five: Two</gloss>

The Dao says: What is spoken within the scripture by the Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning is precisely the "Hidden Sounds of the Inner Names" of the High Emperors of the various heavens. These are also the secret taboo names of the True Kings and the hidden names of the hundred spirits. If the sovereign rulers and marquises of the nations in the ten directions of the world wish to extend their reign through the generations, secure their territories, ensure that the disasters of war do not arise, that floods and droughts do not occur, that theft ceases and the people prosper, and that the seasons follow their desires...

## Chapter on the Divine Transformations of the Great One, the Five Blessings for Protecting the Nation, and the Rituals for Averting Calamity

The Dao says: Formerly, within the Heaven of Beginning Green, in the land of the Great Floating Primordial Void where the songs of the jade-colored sky resound, the <term>Celestial Lord of Primordial Beginning: the highest deity in the Daoist trinity, representing the beginning of the universe</term> received this wondrous chapter on the Divine Transformations of the Great One. As the Celestial Lord spoke this scripture, he repeated it ten times. With each cycle, the Great Spirits of the Heavens, the High Sovereigns and Transcendents, the Perfected Ones of Wondrous Conduct, the True Lords of the <term>Three Primes: refer to the celestial, terrestrial, and water-based divisions of the cosmos</term> and the Great One, and the countless spirits of the Nine Palaces and Eight Officials of the Numinous Charts all arrived through the void. They came riding on carriages of nine-colored light, soaring through the purple mists and red winds. Dragons and mythical beasts formed their procession, and jade-like radiance shimmered in the distance like stars. For nine days and nine nights, the celestial realms were silent, and a numinous wind swept away all impurities, clearing the seas and the lands. The entire nation was bathed in a harmonious light, and the forests and mountains became fragrant and lush. The Celestial Lord sat upon a floating throne of jade and gold, surrounded by jeweled banners and ten thousand dragons.

As he spoke the scripture for the first time <gloss>Heaven Six, One</gloss>, the Great Saints of the various heavens praised the goodness of the teaching. At this time, from the state of primal chaos, existence began to emerge from non-existence.

When he spoke the scripture for the second time <gloss>Two</gloss>, the <term>Great One: Taiyi, a deity representing the primordial unity of the Dao</term> took form, appearing like a lotus seed.

When he spoke the scripture for the third time <gloss>Three</gloss>, golden flowers bloomed and the true breath of the universe flowed like a rainbow.

When he spoke the scripture for the fourth time <gloss>Four</gloss>, nine-colored clouds gathered to form a protective armor.

When he spoke the scripture for the fifth time <gloss>Five</gloss>, the Great One resided in the center, surrounded by the eight celestial wonders.

When he spoke the scripture for the sixth time <gloss>Six</gloss>, the mysterious fluids provided nourishment and the primordial breath acted as an internal support.

When he spoke the scripture for the seventh time <gloss>Seven</gloss>, the "Celestial Infant" underwent seven transformations and was able to make sound.

When he spoke the scripture for the eighth time <gloss>Eight</gloss>, the figure emerged from the "womb" and looked upward.

When he spoke the scripture for the ninth time <gloss>Nine</gloss>, the Great One took his first steps, circling through the Nine Palaces.

When he spoke the scripture for the tenth time <gloss>Ten</gloss>, the deity was clothed in brocade robes and held a jade scepter. At this moment, every man and woman in the nation joyfully watched as the Celestial Lord demonstrated the divine transformations of the Great One, leading them all to long life and salvation.

The Dao says: These "Grotto-Chapters" are the secret sounds of the High Emperors of the various heavens, the ten spirits of the Three Primals and Nine Palaces, the Eight Wonders, the Six Hidden Ones, the Five Truths, the Four Gates, the Two Luminaries, and the Great One of the Primal Beginning. The Dao says: When the cycles of Heaven and Earth approach their end or a period of stagnation, the **True Lord of the Great One** manifests divine transformations to respond. He may appear as a divine horse with a fleshy mane and a single horn, rising and falling within the sea. When the Sun, Moon, and Five Planets are about to suffer an eclipse or fullness, the True Lord of the Great One manifests a divine transformation to respond: he becomes a sorceress, carrying a zither and wandering through the marketplaces. When the most sagely and divine men are about to face success or failure, the Great One manifests a transformation: he becomes a black vapor cutting across East and West, or heavy frost clinging to the trees, or a great wind that destroys and pulls down structures, or a sudden, startling rainstorm. When a student of the lower arts suffers a specific illness or injury, the Great One responds: the student dreams of a bloody corpse, of death in battle, or of falling into a river during a plague. Whenever these disasters appear, observe his divine transformations. Those of the same spirit should align their hearts, cultivate the fast, practice the Way during the six periods of the day, and recite the scripture ten times; merit and blessing will descend immediately. Or, if one encounters the Great One traveling below and offers respectful invitations against the current of the world, one will surely obtain the secret path of the long-lived immortals. Whatever you encounter, observe it with a virtuous mind and do not oppose the spirit; then you shall preserve the correctness of Great Prosperity. This infinite text provides universal salvation without end. <gloss>16</gloss>

The Dao says: For those whose study of the Dao is shallow, or whose immortal rank is not yet full, when their destiny calls for them to pass away and their body undergoes the transition of the **Great Yin** <note>Taiyin: Here referring to the state of "death" in Daoist alchemy where the body is refined in the grave</note>, the True Lord of the Great One who presides over the corpse descends to respond. This is shown through divine transformations: a white crane may fly in, or a tortoise and snake may appear together; or a sudden gale arrives, darkening the sky and earth, while birds and beasts cry out in sorrow, a white rainbow pierces the sun, the mountains and forests change color, and the immortal-to-be experiences strange omens in dreams. Then the Great One guards the corpse, the Three Officials record the soul, and the Nine Elders gather the breath. After one cycle of sixty years <note>Jiazi</note>, the person returns to life and regains their form. Without further effort, they obtain the status of a divine immortal.

The Dao says: When the cycles of Heaven and Earth reach their end, one must also cultivate the fast, burn incense, and recite the scripture. When the constellations are out of alignment and the sun and moon lose their brightness, one must also cultivate the fast, burn incense, and recite the scripture. When the four seasons lose their order and the Yin and Yang are not harmonized, one must also cultivate the fast, burn incense, and recite the scripture. When foreign tribes invade the borders and military actions are violent, one must also cultivate the fast, burn incense, and recite the scripture. When epidemics spread and the people suffer death and injury, one must also cultivate the fast, burn incense, and recite the scripture. When teachers or friends pass away, one must also cultivate the fast, burn incense, and recite the scripture. The merit of fasting and reciting the scripture is extremely heavy. Above, it dissolves celestial disasters and protects the Emperor; below, it repels poisonous harms to deliver the people. Both the living and the dead rely on this blessing; its power is difficult to surpass, thus it is called the Infinite Universal Salvation of Deities and Men. <gloss>17</gloss>

Such a person of high virtue is destined to become a minister of the Golden Gate for the Sage Sovereign. The heavens record human merits and transgressions without the slightest error. # Supreme Wondrous Scripture of the Primordial Infinite Salvation of Mankind — Volume Seven

## Chapter on Manifesting Auspicious Omens and Talismanic Responses

The Dao says: Within the **Heaven of Great Cinnabar** <note>Dadan Tian</note>, above the Realm of the Red Essence in the Grotto-Sun of Obscure Silence, the Primordial One received the "Highest Chapter on Manifesting Auspicious Omens and Talismanic Responses for the Salvation of Mankind." When the **Primordial Heavenly Worthy** <note>Yuanshi Tianzun: The highest deity in the Lingbao tradition</note> was about to speak this scripture, he circled the assembly ten times to summon the Great Spirits of Manifestation from the ten directions. ## First: The Hymn of the Flying Immortals on Primordial Beginning Establishing the Ultimate

Vast and distant, I gaze at the Great Nothingness; 
The many heavens take the Sovereign of the Void as their ancestor. 
The **Longhan** era has already passed; 
In the deep darkness, one is delivered through **Yankang** <note>Longhan and Yankang are the names of previous cosmic aeons</note>. 
Heaven and Earth return to the primordial mists; 
The eight celestial spirits hide their refined light. 
The Three Realms are all dissolved; 
Living beings remain vast and indistinct. 
Only the Realm of the Ultimate Path exists, 
Where those without heavenly cultivation do not go. 
The Red Primal opens the Mysterious Chart; 
The True Text is scattered to the ten directions. 
The Wondrous Breath descends from the Clear Mystery; 
The flying wheels bind the Primal Net. 
The Numinous Treasure nurtures the Three Luminaries; 
The ten thousand transformations are restored and expanded. 
The Mysterious Talisman stabilizes the Jade Mountain; 
The reign of the world shall be without end. 
The High Sages sit within the Circular Net, 
Constantly dwelling in the Hall of Great Blessings. 
They uphold the orthodox path of the Imperial Ultimate, 
Forever entrusting it to the **True Kings**.

## Second: The Chapter of the Great Demons Respectfully Requesting the Preaching of the Scripture

The Mysterious Net is bright and clear, 
Circulating throughout the Eight Voids. 
The wheels turn through the many heavens, 
Gathering at the Mysterious Capital <gloss>Heaven 7</gloss>. 
Solemnly, the ten thousand spirits 
Stand in a circle to attend the Emperor’s dwelling. 
The High Sages spread the ultimate teaching; 
The Cavernous Yang illuminates the bamboo books. 
Ten times the Numinous Chapters are proclaimed <gloss>+</gloss>, 
And all the various beings are brought back to life. 
The Wondrous Dao is limitless and extreme; 
A single pearl is hidden within the billion heavens. 
The Immortals and Perfected celebrate without end; 
The Jade Void receives the Mysterious Talisman. 
The Red Script shines in the blue-green sky; 
Auspicious smoke floats, filling the void. 
The Great Earth brings forth precious sounds; 
The stunted trees produce jade-like gems. 
The Phoenix and Qilin descend to the world; 
The Jade Mushrooms flourish in the corners of the courtyard. 
Through ten thousand kalpas, peace is attained; 
The Mysterious Transformation is spread from this moment.

## Third: The Proclamation of the True Emperors on the Response of Auspicious Talismans

The Sovereign of the Primal Void 
Dwells high within the Jade Purity. 
He gives birth to and nurtures the Three Luminaries, 
Establishing the roots of Heaven. 
To the right, the Mysterious Brilliance is arrayed; 
To the left, the light of the sun and moon is carried. 
Dividing the breath, it descends to the Middle Heaven; 
The **Northern Dipper** (Douji) is the most supreme. 
He sits auspiciously, receiving the eight directions; 
Below, he responds to the human sovereign. 
When the human sovereign follows the Way of Heaven, 
Excellent omens arise according to his virtue. 
The Earth brings forth the Register of Long Life; 
Heaven bestows the Text of the Mysterious Scenery. 
The mountains and rivers float with elegant breath; 
Precious wonders gather at the royal court. 
The millions of people suffer no disasters; 
The five grains are guaranteed a bountiful harvest. 
Brightly proclaim the will of the **Most High**; 
Let all the myriad heavens hear it. 
All the various beings are filled with joy; 
They bow their heads, burdened by the Mysterious Grace.

This is the song of the **True Demons** within the flying void above the Three Realms; its sound joins with the Chapters of the Cavern. If recited one hundred times, one’s name is recorded in the **Southern Palace** <note>The office of rebirth and immortality</note>. Recited one thousand times, the True Demons will protect and welcome you. Recited ten thousand times, the Dao is complete and one ascends to the Great Void, passing through the Three Realms to attain the rank of Immortal Duke. I possess the Numinous Sound and the Heavenly Omens; when they descend to the body, the Demon Kings respect the form and follow the commands. The Earth Spirits stand guard and escort you <gloss>Heaven 7</gloss> <gloss>+</gloss>. They welcome and pull you out from the "corpses of the earth" <note>The state of death and decay</note> and the five sufferings and eight hardships. The ancestors of seven generations will rise and return, eternally leaving the Dark Bureau. Their souls will cross the **Zhu Ling** <note>The Palace of Vermilion Fire/Southern Palace where souls are refined</note>, undergo refinement, and be reborn. This is called the Limitless Universal Salvation. It contains the secret texts of the Upper Heavens, which are honored by all the heavens. To leak them or treat them with slow disrespect will lead to hell, and the disaster will reach even back to the grandfather of one's seven ancestors.

The Dao says: These three chapters are the most numinous and hidden secret sounds of the Emperors of the various heavens.

The breath of the **Upper Primal Great Harmony and Myriad Blessings** manifests as auspicious omens and signs. It is revealed to the Sovereign through the presence of loyal, worthy, and wise ministers. Among physical objects, it manifests as precious jade and rarities. Among animals, it appears as the **Qilin, Phoenix, Turtle, and Dragon** <note>The four benevolent spiritual animals of Chinese mythology</note>. Upon the earth, it manifests as the **Five Fungi** <note>Magical mushrooms/lingzhi that signify immortality</note>, strange trees, precious stones, and the auspiciousness of mountains and rivers. In the heavens, it appears as celebratory clouds, bright stars, and sweet dew. 

When the Human Sovereign possesses the Dao, the talismans respond to the virtue of his actions. These are all the words of the **Great Brahma** <note>Dafan; referring to the primal, celestial language of the highest heavens, which predates human speech</note>; they are not the common phrases of the world, nor are they rhythmic verses or flowery songs. Because they are mysterious and profound, they are difficult to investigate in detail. They are the treasures of the upper heavens, kept secret in the **Eastern Scripture Room of the Royal Palace of the Divine Zenith and Jade Purity**. They are circulated and transmitted downward only when the cosmic cycles <note>specifically the Ren-Chen year</note> correspond. If there is a person of ultimate virtue, they must first offer gold and jewels as a pledge of their heart, following the ancient rules and swearing an oath to the **Three Heavens**, before these teachings may be bestowed.

The Dao says: When one practices the virtues of goodness and benevolence, Heaven reveals auspicious talismans to reward the Sovereign. When one commits the sins of evil and extravagance, Heaven reveals disasters and anomalies to warn the people. Therefore, when the cycles of Heaven and Earth reach their end, or when the sun, moon, and five planets lose their balance—the divine man understands these periods of success and failure. When common scholars encounter such disasters, those who share the same breath should join their hearts to practice the **Zhai** <note>Ritual fasting and purification</note>. They should offer incense at the six appointed hours and circumambulate while reciting the scripture ten times. Auspicious omens will immediately descend, all misfortunes will be extinguished, and the Limitless Text shall universally deliver without end.
